prediction_ref.short_label: MCP specification makes remote-server authentication mandatory by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's LiteLLM exploitation is the strongest pressure yet behind mandatory MCP authentication. Per the CISA-KEV story, the flaw lives in two unauthenticated test endpoints (POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list) that accept a full server config and spawn it as a subprocess on the proxy host with no validation, yielding remote code execution with "no login, no API key, and no prior access." The remediation framing - authenticate every caller, keep the MCP-config layer off the public internet - is exactly the unauthenticated-by-default failure mode that a mandatory-authentication change to the MCP spec would close. This is a real-world demonstration that the spec's optional auth is being exploited.
